title: A shilling's cab to Charing Cross
learning_goal: Know the cab, the fare, the times, and that Fogg does not take the nine-year-old Underground; feel cobbles and hooves.

narration.script: Down to the end of Savile Row and into a cab — a hansom, most likely; Verne never says. To the cabby, Fogg is a swell, and the fare is sixpence a mile or part of one; it is barely a mile and a half to Charing Cross — call it a bob. Watch the line on the 1872 map, south and east to Trafalgar Square and the Strand. London already had an Underground — nine years old, steam-hauled and smoky. Fogg takes a cab. Listen: hooves on stone, and an Offenbach galop, because Passepartout is a Parisian and would want one. They left the club at twenty-five past seven. They are at Charing Cross at twenty past eight.

production_notes: Slang comes only from the 1874 All the Year Round list and the money terms in F-31. Cab type: 'a hansom, most likely' — Verne never names it (F-12 note, F-28). Distance: ≈ 1.6 km by road (~1 mile), 6d a mile or part of one, 1s minimum on the 1871 tariff — 'call it a bob' (F-28, fact-check). No 'wet' anywhere before Quiz B (R5) — the rain arrives with the platform. accessibility.sound_captions = caption-track entries for sound-only cues (not overlays; they do not count against overlay density). Linear cut: 40 s — trim the Underground line and the Offenbach aside.
